population.method: Each 2021 neighbourhood population is divided by the total massing floor area in that neighbourhood (all buildings), then assigned to buildings in the section by floor area x use weight (residential/unknown 1, mixed 0.5, non-residential 0). Floors = average height / 3.2 m.
limits: Residential population only; no daytime, worker, student or visitor population
Building use is from OSM tags where present; untagged buildings are assumed residential
University neighbourhood includes the U of T campus, which lowers its per-floor density
Do not present cell values as census counts

signal_timing.why: The City timing dataset is a phase-status snapshot without phase durations, so cycle and split lengths are not observed. It does confirm phase 2/6 (Bloor) and 4/8 (cross street) with pedestrian phases at the Bloor signals.
signal_timing.pedestrian_speed_source: Observed PEDWALKSPEED attribute on each signal: 1.0 m/s (flashing do-not-walk based on 1.2 m/s)

rules.rule: An agent moves only along edges that permit its current mode: walk on sidewalks and crosswalks, bike in the cycle track (or a car lane where no track exists), drive in car lanes, ride transit between stops of a scheduled vehicle.
Position changes only by traversing edges at the mode speed, capped by congestion; no jumps.
Changing side of Bloor is allowed only on a crosswalk that crosses Bloor. Signalized crosswalks may be entered only during the walk interval of the matching phase. Mid-block crossing is rejected.
Cars, buses and cyclists stop at a red for their movement and proceed in arrival order on green.
Transit is boarded only at a station platform or stop when a scheduled departure (GTFS) arrives; the fare is charged by the fare rules in data/ttc_fare_context.json.
A purchase or visit happens only after the agent reaches the building door and the business is open. No sales by narration.
Each agent has a money budget and a schedule; a late arrival to a fixed appointment is recorded as a cost.
Agents observe their own edge, the next signal state, and transit arrival predictions, but never global state.

Actions come from a fixed menu (walk_to, bike_to, drive_to, take_transit, wait, enter, purchase, skip_trip). The Game Master validates every action; invalid actions fall back to a default rule and are logged.
Baseline and policy runs start from the same seed, people, schedule, weather and background flow.

policy_levers.effect: none removes the cycle-track edges; cyclists then share the car lane edges
capacity of the Bloor car-lane edges
curbside stopping for pickups and deliveries

assumptions.note: Cycle, splits and offsets are assumed (see signal_timing).
Schematic offsets: car lanes at y = +/-3 m, cycle tracks at +/-7 m, sidewalks at +/-12 m. Lane counts and cycleway types come from OSM tags.
Walk 1.2 m/s (signal crossing 1.0 m/s observed), bike 4.5 m/s, car free-flow 40 km/h posted limit.
Untagged OSM buildings count as residential; with a business inside they count as mixed.
Residents per building are a dasymetric estimate (see population.method).

limits: Counts are one weekday (2025-06-25), 14 hours; not an annual average
Background flow reproduces observed counts by construction; only agent behaviour and the policy run are simulated
Business presence from OSM; no revenue, staffing, or closure data
Scheduled transit, not observed reliability or crowding
This world is a 619 m section; do not scale its outputs to the corridor or the city
